items.summary: 전남광주 나주에서 60대 부부가 결박된 상태로 숨진 채 발견된 사건과 관련해 경찰이 집 주변 폐쇄회로(CC)TV 영상 속 한 남성을 유력한 용의자로 보고 이틀째 추적하고 있다.7일 나주경찰서에 따르면 전날 오후 7시49분께 나주시 왕곡면 한 주택에서 60대 A씨 부부가 숨진 채 발견됐다는 신고가 접수됐다.현장에 출동한 경찰은 집 안에서 옷가지 등에 발이 묶인 채 숨져 있는 A씨 부부를 발견했다.경찰의 1차 검시 결과 남편은 흉기에 찔려 숨진 외인사, 부인은 기도 폐쇄에 따른 질식사로 추정됐다.경찰은 이들 부부가 발견 전날인 지난 5일 밤부터 6일 오후 사이 살해된 것으로 보고 있다. 범행에 사용된 것으로 추정되는 흉기는 현장에서 발견되지 않았다.경찰은 집 주변 CCTV에서 한 남성의 모습을 확인, 유력한 용의자로 보고 행방을 쫒고 있다. 아직 용의자 신원은 특정되지 않았다.경찰은 A씨를 검거하는 대로 정확한 범행 동기와 경위 등을 조사할 방침이다.[전남광주=뉴시스]

items.title: 맑고 쌀쌀한 출근길…강원 일부 얼음·서리
items.summary: 수요일인 7일은 대체로 맑은 가운데 아침 기온이 크게 떨어져 쌀쌀하겠다. 전국 대부분 지역에서 낮과 밤의 기온 차가 15도 안팎까지 크게 벌어지겠다.기상청에 따르면 당분간 기온은 평년과 비슷하거나 조금 낮겠다.특히 북서쪽에서 찬 공기가 유입되면서 강원도 일부 지역에는 한파 특보가 발효되고, 강원 산지에는 얼음이 어는 곳도 있겠다. 일부 강원내륙·산지와 경북 북동 산지에 서리가 내리는 곳도 있겠다.이날 아침 최저기온은 3~14도, 낮 최고기온은 21~25도로 예보됐다.주요 도시별 예상 아침 최저기온은 △서울 11도 △인천 12도 △춘천 5도 △강릉 11도 △대전 10도 △대구 11도 △전주 11도 △광주 11도 △부산 14도 △제주 18도다.낮 최고기온은 △서울 24도 △인천 23도 △춘천 22도 △강릉 21도 △대전 23도 △대구 24도 △전주 24도 △광주 25도 △부산 25도 △제주 24도로 예상된다.새벽부터 오전 사이 강원내륙·산지에 짙은 안개가 끼는 곳이 있겠다.

items.title: Starwatch: how to spot Saturn as it makes it closest approach to Earth this year
items.summary: The planet looks like a moderately bright, creamy-white object and is easily visible to the naked eye This week offers an excellent opportunity to track down Saturn. The giant planet, situated about 10 times further from the sun than the Earth, reached opposition on 4 October. In this configuration, Earth is passing almost directly between the planet and the sun. This makes opposition an excellent time to see a planet: the distant world rises as the sun sets, remains visible throughout the night and sets around sunrise. articles.title: The west has a blinkered view of African music – and it’s hurting the whole continent’s culture
articles.snippet: The term Afrobeats is applied to all sorts of genres, flattening them into one. Artists, media and the music industry must do better at showing off the richness of African pop In 2024, South African pop star Tyla won the best Afrobeats award at the MTV VMAs. Beaming in a yellow dress, she began her acceptance speech in a celebratory tone. “This is such a big moment for African music. The global impact of Water,” – her hit single – “proves that African music can be pop music.” But as the audience’s cheers swelled, she became more sombre, describing the moment as bittersweet. “There’s a tendency to group all African music as Afrobeats,” she continued. “Even though Afrobeats has opened so many doors for us, African music is so diverse. I come from South Africa, I represent amapiano”, referring to the country’s rolling, sensual dance subgenre. Her passionate entreaty notwithstanding, months later she’d reprise her win in the Afrobeats category of the American Music Awards. Tyla is hardly the only African artist to rail against the Afrobeats tag. Tems has spurned the term, describing her music as a cocktail of “Afro, R&B, soul and alternative elements”. Likewise, Burna Boy prefers to call his music Afrofusion, a fitting characterisation of the smorgasbord of sounds that converge in his music. Wizkid, Ckay, King Promise and Davido have also chafed at the term Afrobeats, yet it persists and holds back African music. Continue reading...

articles.title: Silver Pines review – a stylish, neo-noir detective drama
articles.snippet: PC, PS5, Switch 2; Wych Elm Games, Team 17 Abandoned shops, ruined apartment buildings and rotting sewer networks make up a dark landscape in which you play a private eye searching for a missing singer-songwriter In a weird deserted town miles from anywhere, a troubled detective searches for a missing musician and the girl he may or may not have murdered. It could be a Silent Hill game or a lost David Lynch movie from the 1990s – in fact, it’s neither. And also both. If that whets your appetite, stick around, there’s plenty more to come. Developed by Scandinavian studio Wych Elm Games, Silver Pines is a dark Metroidvania-style adventure, where you play as shambling private eye, Red Walker, exploring a 2D universe of abandoned shops, ruined apartment buildings and rotting sewer networks. Officially, everyone has left because of an incoming storm, but very quickly you learn that something much darker is afoot. Someone has hired you to find singer-songwriter Eddie Velvet, but you don’t know why; your only contact with your client is via the payphones dotted around town, where you can also save your progress – as long as you have a dollar to pay for the call. Each location is filled with clues and puzzles – a weird newspaper story pinned to the wall, a strange statue that needs a missing piece – and through these artefacts you unlock new rooms and descend further into the mystery. articles.title: V/H/S/Mixtape review – murderous puppets pull the strings in mixed bag of gory music-themed mini-movies
articles.snippet: Metal band Gwar host this instalment of the horror series, which serves up darkly humorous movie morsels that would struggle to frighten a toddler The latest in the long-running horror-feature series is, as per usual, a decidedly diverse ragbag of shorts, strung together with the thinnest of connective tissue. The theme this go-round seems to be music and sound, so it sort of makes sense that hosting duties for the interstitial bits fall to the goofy metal band Gwar, its assorted members met here cracking Halloween dad jokes in their trademark extravagant outfits. The five mini movies vary significantly in length as well as quality. Flying Lotus’s stop-motion exercise Another Cabin posits a young boy in a rural cabin living with a mean old grannie who tries to push him forward when a tentacled demon tears the roof of the house in search of a snack. The characters’ resemblance to the cast of early 2000s series The PJs is slightly jarring, given this is such a different register, but the brevity works in its favour. In contrast Renee Zhan’s Dance, Dance, Dance, Dance, the opener, drags on a bit, but has a reasonable gags-to-gore ratio in its tale of murderous puppets taking revenge on visiting studio execs who would dare to “reimagine” some ageing IP best left dormant. The funniest gag is the bright major-scale title song the puppets (designed by Jim Henson’s Creature Shop) sing about how all things must die. Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘Exceptionally crafted’: why Little Shop of Horrors is my feelgood movie
articles.snippet: The latest in our series of writers’ favorite comfort films is a tribute to the lovably quirky 80s musical The key to a feelgood movie, beyond the necessary rewatchability, is familiarity – the real kind that lets you look away or fall asleep without doubting your affection. Musicals are perfectly suited to this particular subgenre since the majority of them, especially the classic ones adapted for film, atrophy with second-act problems. That’s where writers suddenly remember the plot they had introduced and drop all that singing and dancing to arrive at some type of conclusion. The first act of Funny Girl? A near-flawless parade of showstoppers, Barbra Streisand as Fanny Brice having the time of her life falling in love. I’ve probably seen it 200 times. The second act … well, who ever cared about her husband’s gambling addiction? Continue reading...

articles.title: Kemi Badenoch is the most rightwing leader in Tory history. Isn’t it time she got some actual scrutiny? | Owen Jones
articles.snippet: Farage’s scandals have allowed Badenoch to get her party back in the race. But her programme would be no less ruinous for our country The Conservative leader, Kemi Badenoch, will march on to the conference stage in Birmingham feeling buoyed. “Kemi’s soaring,” coos the Sun, and that sums up the prevailing wisdom. More than four in 10 Britons think she is doing well as Tory leader, compared with a third who think otherwise. As Nigel Farage’s stock has plummeted thanks to scandals over a £5m personal gift and donations from crypto billionaires, the polling suggests that the Conservatives could regain the mantle of Britain’s main rightwing force. Yet Badenoch has been the beneficiary of circumstance. Her tenure as opposition leader has been defined by Keir Starmer’s project imploding almost as soon as it gained power. When Reform UK enjoyed its seismic polling lead, the Tory plight was double-edged: they were starved of attention, but that inevitably resulted in a lack of scrutiny, too. It has been easy for Badenoch to appear formidable while her opponents have disintegrated. Owen Jones is a Guardian columnist Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? articles.title: Burnham’s surprise EU-turn could deliver the Tories from a generational mess | Gaby Hinsliff
articles.snippet: Badenoch would never have reopened the door on Brexit, but now that the PM has, it suits the Conservatives to let him walk through it There’s no way on earth it should have worked, but somehow he may have got away with it. Last week, the actor Richard E Grant became the first contestant on The Traitors – a show whose only unbreakable rule is never to let anyone know you’re the murderer – to gleefully announce within minutes of being selected that yes, haha, it’s him! Yet even then many of his fellow contestants seemed to like him too much to recoil. And that, roughly speaking, is now Andy Burnham’s Brexit strategy. After years of Labour politicians – not least Burnham himself, in the Makerfield byelection, without which he would not now be prime minister – trying to hide their real feelings about Brexit, Burnham has decided just to tell the truth and hope people roll with it. Leaving hasn’t worked, he said bluntly last week in Liverpool, and Britain should consider the alternatives. If you’re a leaver who suspects him of being out to unwind Brexit – well, yes, he is. This bold strategy seemingly surprised much of his own cabinet, an early lesson in how he likes to work for those who hadn’t studied his Manchester operation closely enough. But the oddly muted initial response to what would once have been a seismic shock suggests it’s wrongfooting some opponents, too. Gaby Hinsliff is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

articles.title: The Guardian view on Tory economics: Britain’s future needs more than Thatcher’s past | Editorial
articles.snippet: The Conservatives blame their failures on abandoning their 1976 principles. But the country needs investment and resilience rather than another round of spending cuts The Conservative party wants to go back to the future under Kemi Badenoch. In her foundational text, The Right Way, released at the weekend, the Tory party leader makes its intellectual lineage explicit, repeatedly invoking Margaret Thatcher’s 1976 policy statement The Right Approach. The 2026 economic framework is familiar: only private enterprise creates wealth; taxes, regulation and spending can obstruct growth and competition; markets make the country stronger. The speech by her shadow chancellor, Andrew Griffith, made it clear that Conservative failures over its 14-year spell in charge were the result of the party straying from Thatcherite principles. One might argue that, on the contrary, errors were because the party slavishly followed such a creed. When Rough, a depleted North Sea gasfield that once provided around 70% of the UK’s gas-storage capacity, was judged uneconomic by its private owner, a Conservative government in 2017 accepted that international markets could provide the UK with adequate energy security. That proved to be a big mistake when Russia invaded Ukraine, sending fossil fuel prices upwards. Britain was particularly exposed as a net energy importer and highly dependent on gas. Tory ministers had to bring back Rough into operation in 2022. Mrs Badenoch puts its closure down to “false economies”. But what was wrong was putting private profitability ahead of the country’s needs. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article?
